I'll start by exploring both repos to understand the mirror create flow and where the suspension check needs to happen.

158				}
159				owner, repo, err := parseGitHubURL(args[0])
160				if err != nil {

162					return fmt.Errorf("invalid <github-url>: %w", err)
163				}

166				// cluster guessing is intentionally limited to the interactive
167				// wizard (the no-args path above), so scripts get stable behavior.
168				clusterHost := clusterArg(args)
169				if err := validateClusterHost(clusterHost); err != nil {
170					cmd.SilenceUsage = true
171					return fmt.Errorf("invalid [cluster-host]: %w", err)
172				}
173				return runCoreForCluster(cmd, clusterHost, func(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client) error {
174					errW := cmd.ErrOrStderr()
175					stop := startSpinner(errW, fmt.Sprintf("Cloning %s/%s into %s", owner, repo, clusterHost))
176					// nil onStatus: the one-shot's single spinner shows liveness; the
177					// per-mirror progress lines are the wizard's concern.
178					outcome, err := createAndAwaitMirror(ctx, c, owner, repo, clusterHost, noWait, waitTimeout, nil)
179					// Only a confirmed-ready clone earns the ✓; everything else
180					// (empty, --no-wait, suspended, failed, timeout) erases the line

182					stop(err == nil && outcome.polled && outcome.status == coreapi.MirrorStatusReady)

192	// mirrorCreateOutcome bundles the create response with the clone status
193	// observed while waiting. polled is false for --no-wait and for empty upstreams,
194	// where there is nothing to await; in those cases status is unset.
195	type mirrorCreateOutcome struct {
196		created *coreapi.CreatedMirror
197		status  coreapi.MirrorStatus
198		polled  bool
199	}
200	
201	// createAndAwaitMirror is the single create-then-wait path shared by the
202	// `repo mirror create <github-url>` one-shot and the onboarding wizard, so both
203	// report identical lifecycle states. It registers the GitHub mirror on
204	// clusterHost (idempotent on (upstream, cluster)) and, unless noWait or the
205	// upstream is empty, polls the control plane until the clone reaches a terminal
206	// status. The returned error is the create error (when outcome.created is nil)
207	// or the wait error — a status sentinel (errMirrorCloneFailed /
208	// errMirrorSuspended) or a timeout; callers read outcome.status for the state.
209	func createAndAwaitMirror(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client, owner, repo, clusterHost string, noWait bool, timeout time.Duration, onStatus func(coreapi.MirrorStatus)) (mirrorCreateOutcome, error) {
210		created, err := c.CreateMirror(ctx, &coreapi.CreateMirrorInputBody{
211			Provider:    coreapi.CreateMirrorInputBodyProviderGithub,
212			Owner:       owner,
213			Repo:        repo,
214			ClusterHost: clusterHost,
215		})
216		if err != nil {
217			return mirrorCreateOutcome{}, err
218		}
219		outcome := mirrorCreateOutcome{created: created}
220		if created.Empty {
221			// An empty upstream has nothing to clone, so don't poll for "ready" — it
222			// never would. But an *existing* placement can be suspended even when
223			// empty, and one status read surfaces that (a fresh create can't be
224			// suspended — suspension follows upstream access loss). Mirrors the old
225			// finishMirrorCreate behavior; the read is best-effort, so a transient
226			// GetMirror error just falls through to the benign "nothing to clone".
227			if !created.Created {
228				if m, gerr := c.GetMirror(ctx, coreapi.GetMirrorParams{MirrorId: created.MirrorId}); gerr == nil {
229					if s, ok := m.Status.Get(); ok && s == coreapi.MirrorStatusSuspended {
230						outcome.status = s
231						outcome.polled = true
232						return outcome, errMirrorSuspended
233					}
234				}
235			}
236			return outcome, nil
237		}
238		if noWait {
239			return outcome, nil
240		}
241		status, werr := awaitMirrorReady(ctx, c, created.MirrorId, timeout, onStatus)
242		outcome.status = status
243		outcome.polled = true
244		return outcome, werr
245	}
246	
247	// reportOneShotMirror renders the human output for `repo mirror create
248	// <github-url>` from the shared createAndAwaitMirror result. A nil
249	// outcome.created means CreateMirror itself failed — surface that error (nothing
250	// was printed yet). Otherwise echo the placement, then the lifecycle outcome.
251	func reportOneShotMirror(out, errW io.Writer, outcome mirrorCreateOutcome, err error) error {
252		created := outcome.created
253		if created == nil {
254			return err
255		}
256		if created.Created {
257			fmt.Fprintf(out, "Registered mirror %s\n", created.MirrorId)
258		} else {
259			fmt.Fprintf(out, "Mirror already exists (%s)\n", created.MirrorId)
260		}
261		fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", created.MirrorUrl)
262	
263		if !outcome.polled {
264			if created.Empty {
265				fmt.Fprintln(out, "Upstream has no commits yet — nothing to clone. The mirror will pick up refs once the upstream is pushed to.")
266			} else {
267				fmt.Fprintf(out, "Initial clone may still be in progress; `git clone %s` will work once it completes.\n", created.MirrorUrl)
268			}
269			return nil
270		}
271	
272		switch outcome.status {
273		case coreapi.MirrorStatusReady:
274			fmt.Fprintf(out, "\nClone it:\n  git clone %s\n", created.MirrorUrl)
275			return nil
276		case coreapi.MirrorStatusSuspended:
277			explainSuspendedMirror(errW, created.MirrorId)
278			return NewSilentError(errMirrorSuspended)
279		case coreapi.MirrorStatusFailed:
280			return fmt.Errorf("initial clone of mirror %s failed", created.MirrorId)
281		case coreapi.MirrorStatusProcessing:
282			// Still processing when the poll returned: the wait timed out (or a
283			// transport error broke the poll). awaitMirrorReady's err carries which.
284			return err
285		default:
286			return err
287		}
288	}

106	//

108	// live per-mirror progress (e.g. the wizard's Docker-style line list).
109	func awaitMirrorReady(ctx context.Context, c mirrorStatusGetter, mirrorID string, timeout time.Duration, onStatus func(coreapi.MirrorStatus)) (coreapi.MirrorStatus, error) {

116		defer ticker.Stop()

122			switch {

go test $RACE $VERBOSE -timeout "$TIMEOUT" $packages

for gomod in modules/*/go.mod; do
  [ -e "$gomod" ] || continue
  mod=$(dirname "$gomod")
  echo "=== $mod ==="
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  ( cd "$mod" && go vet ./... && go test $RACE $VERBOSE -timeout "$TIMEOUT" ./... )
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#MISE description="Verify simulation tests produce deterministic output"

set -o errexit
set -o nounset
set -o pipefail

#USAGE flag "-t --test_seed <seed>" help="Test seed (default: 12345)"
#USAGE flag "--test <name>" help="Test to run (default: TestLeaderStatusAfterRestart)"

SEED=${usage_test_seed:-12345}
TEST_NAME=${usage_test:-TestRepairScaleUp}
TIMEOUT="10m"

export ENTIRE_REFSTORE_BACKEND=postgresql
export ENTIRE_POSTGRES_DSN="REDACTED"

echo "Verifying determinism: $TEST_NAME with seed=$SEED"

# Generate overlay JSON
go run ./internal/sim/cmd/gen-overlay -o internal/sim/overlay.json

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

run_test() {
  local output_file=$1
  GOGC=off GOMAXPROCS=1 GODEBUG=asyncpreemptoff=1 TEST_SEED="$SEED" \
    go test -v -count=1 -timeout "$TIMEOUT" \
    -overlay=internal/sim/overlay.json -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 \
    -tags sim_deterministic \
    -run "^${TEST_NAME}\$" ./test/simulation 2>&1 \
    | grep -v '"time"' \
    | sed -E 's/^(--- (PASS|FAIL): [^ ]+) \([0-9]+\.[0-9]+s\)$/\1/' \
    | sed -E 's/^(ok  	[^ ]+)	[0-9]+\.[0-9]+s$/\1/' \
    > "$output_file"
}

echo "Run 1..."
run_test "$tmpdir/run1.log"

echo "Run 2..."
run_test "$tmpdir/run2.log"

if diff -u "$tmpdir/run1.log" "$tmpdir/run2.log" > "$tmpdir/diff.log" 2>&1; then
  echo "PASS: Both runs produced identical output (excluding timestamps)"
else
  echo "FAIL: Runs diverged!"
  echo "--- diff ---"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#MISE description="Run the OIDF conformance suite against entire-core (containerized) and assert vs baseline"

# Brings the whole topology up on one docker network (CockroachDB + SpiceDB +
# NATS + entire-core OP + mock-IdP + the certified OIDF suite), runs the
# curated plans, diffs the verdicts against test/conformance/oidf/baseline.json,
# and tears everything down. The suite's own headless browser drives the login
# leg — no external driver, no /etc/hosts.
#
#   mise run test:oidf-conformance                  # run + assert (fails on delta)
#   mise run test:oidf-conformance -- --update-baseline   # calibrate the baseline

set -o errexit
set -o nounset
set -o pipefail

ROOT="${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}"
DIR="$ROOT/test/conformance/oidf"
# Overlay the conformance stack on the repo-root compose so the base `core` +
# `nats` infra is reused. --project-directory pins relative-path resolution to
# the repo root for both files.
COMPOSE=(docker compose --project-directory "$ROOT"
  -f "$ROOT/docker-compose.yml" -f "$DIR/docker-compose.yml"
  --profile core --profile nats)
SUITE_URL="${OIDF_SUITE_URL:-https://localhost:9443}"  # nginx publishes host :9443 -> container :8443

# shellcheck disable=SC2329  # invoked indirectly via the EXIT trap
cleanup() {
  local rc=$?
  # On any failure (a crashed container, a stuck suite, a baseline delta) dump
  # status + logs before tearing down — `up -d` detaches, so without this a
  # container that exits during startup leaves no trace in CI.
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "==> Run failed (exit $rc) — container status + logs:" >&2
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" ps 2>&1 || true
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" logs --no-color --tail=200 \
      entire-core entire-mock-idp nats spicedb cockroachdb server browser-driver 2>&1 || true
  fi
  echo "==> Tearing down the OIDF conformance stack"
  "${COMPOSE[@]}" down -v --remove-orphans >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "==> Ensuring the dev TLS bundle exists (mkcert via dev:ssl-setup; idempotent)"
mise run dev:ssl-setup
# mkcert writes private keys 0600 owned by the host user, but entire-core runs
# as non-root (uid 1000) and reads them over a bind mount. On Linux that's a
# hard "permission denied" (Docker Desktop's file sharing masks it locally), so
# make the throwaway dev key material world-readable for the container.
chmod a+r "$ROOT"/certs/*.pem

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#MISE description="Run simulation tests with deterministic scheduling"

set -o errexit
set -o nounset
set -o pipefail

#USAGE flag "--verbose" help="Verbose output"
#USAGE flag "-t --test_seed <seed>" help="Test seed"
#USAGE flag "-p --parallel <n>" help="Max simultaneous sim tests (default: nproc)"

export ENTIRE_REFSTORE_BACKEND=postgresql
export ENTIRE_POSTGRES_DSN="REDACTED"

VERBOSE_FLAG=""
TIMEOUT="10m"
if [ "${usage_verbose:-false}" = "true" ]; then
  VERBOSE_FLAG="-test.v"
fi

export TEST_SEED=${usage_test_seed:-}

# Each sim test runs in its own process: synctest requires fresh global state,
# and GOMAXPROCS=1 + asyncpreemptoff=1 + seeded runtime PRNG give deterministic
# scheduling per process. Compile the binary once so we don't pay go-test
# build + linker startup 18×.
WORK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK_DIR"' EXIT
SIM_BIN="$WORK_DIR/sim.test"

# Generate overlay JSON with correct GOROOT path
go run ./internal/sim/cmd/gen-overlay -o internal/sim/overlay.json

go test -c -o "$SIM_BIN" \
  -overlay=internal/sim/overlay.json -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 \
  -tags sim_deterministic \
  ./test/simulation

# Each sim test pins itself to GOMAXPROCS=1, so N parallel processes use ~N cores.
PARALLEL="${usage_parallel:-}"
if [ -z "$PARALLEL" ]; then
  PARALLEL=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu 2>/dev/null || echo 4)
fi

run_one() {
  local name=$1
  echo "Running $name..."
  GOMAXPROCS=1 GODEBUG=asyncpreemptoff=1 \
    "$SIM_BIN" $VERBOSE_FLAG -test.timeout "$TIMEOUT" -test.run "^${name}\$"
}
